From: ops@globex.com

Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy: key rotation expectations and ephemeral keys

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off our on-prem pilot with Redwood and the security/compliance team at GlobeBank has a couple of questions before we complete the SOW. Specifically:

- We want a clear runbook that describes how BYOK is ingested, where primary keys live (HSM vs operator), and exactly how ephemeral session keys are derived and rotated.
- Auditability: what artifacts are produced to prove rotations happened (timestamps, signer, rotation reason), and how long those artifacts are retained?
- Can Redwood support a nightly ephemeral-key rotation for tenant kernels, and is there a safe rollback plan if rotation fails mid-window?

Can you point us to an example runbook or share a short summary? Our compliance team is on standby; if useful we can set a short call.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Ops Lead, Globex Integration
ops@globex.com
(attachment: redacted-scope.pdf)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: ops@globex.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: key rotation expectations and ephemeral keys

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the list. Short answer: yes, we support an operator-held BYOK flow backed by an HSM while issuing short-lived tenant session keys (ephemeral keys) per workload. Ive attached a draft runbook (redwood-kms-ephemeral-runbook-v1.pdf) and architecture diagram for your review. Highlights up front:

- BYOK ingestion: customer imports a root wrapping key into their HSM. Redwood never persists plaintext root keys. We perform a one-time envelope wrap with the on-prem HSM and store only the wrapped key material in the control plane.
- Ephemeral keys: each tenant session receives a derived ephemeral symmetric key (AES-256), valid for a configurable window (default 24 hours). Keys are derived using HKDF with tenant-specific salt and a per-rotation nonce.
- Rotation cadence: default daily for ephemeral keys; customer can request hourly or weekly depending on throughput and audit policy.
- Fail-safe: rotations are two-stage — pre-provision (dry-run) then cutover. If a cutover fails, previous ephemerals remain valid until TTL expiry; we also support immediate rollback by re-enabling prior key bundle.
- Audit artifacts: rotation events emit signed rotation records (rotation_id, timestamp, operator identity, pre/post key version hashes) and are written to local audit log plus optional remote syslog collector. Retention is configurable; default: 90 days on appliance, longer in S3 archive via customer's storage.

Can your compliance team skim the attached and flag any showstoppers? I'll loop in Dylan and Mina to fill in operational steps and L3 rollback runbook.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
(attachment: redwood-kms-ephemeral-runbook-v1.pdf, kms-architecture-diagram.png)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ops@globex.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-23T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: operator run steps and CLI snippets for rotation

Alex / Soojin —

I reviewed the runbook and dropped a concise operator checklist below for nightly rotations. Please treat these as a draft for discussion. I can convert to a playbook page if this layout works.

Operator nightly rotation (recommended flow):
1) Preflight: run `redwoodctl kms preflight --tenant <TENANT_ID> --check-integrity` to validate HSM reachability and wrapped-key fingerprint.
2) Dry-run generation: `redwoodctl kms generate-ephemeral --tenant <TENANT_ID> --preview --nonce <RANDOM>` — stores ephemeral key in staging slot and emits rotation preview file (rotation_id + hash).
3) Sync checks: verify consumers have preloaded KV-cache shards. If cache misses > 2% during preview, abort.
4) Cutover: `redwoodctl kms rotate --tenant <TENANT_ID> --rotation-id <RID>` — changes active ephemeral pointer atomically across N replicas.
5) Post-check: monitor token auth success rate for 30 minutes. If errors > 0.5% then trigger rollback: `redwoodctl kms rollback --tenant <TENANT_ID> --rotation-id <PREV_RID>`.

Notes on telemetry/audit: each command writes a signed envelope to /var/log/redwood/kms/audit.log and emits a JSON event to the control-plane audit API. We sign rotation audit records with the HSM key and include the operator principal.

I'll attach CLI examples and a minimal JSON schema for the audit record in the next drop.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: cli-examples.txt)

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: ops@globex.com
Date: 2027-05-23T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: L3 rollback details + HSM key lifecycle notes

Quick clarifications for GlobeBank compliance team:

- HSM custody: customer-managed HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 / Level 4 depending on device) holds the root wrapping key. Redwood signs rotation events with a separate signing key stored in the same HSM under a different slot to ensure separation of duties.
- Key split: we support threshold-splitting for root key custody if required. Operator access requires multi-person approval; we integrate with YubiHSM/KMS providers and can map to KMIP where supported.
- Proof of rotation: rotation audit record contains rotation_id, pre-hash, post-hash, operator principal, HSM signature, and a short explanation field. Export format: gzipped JSON + detached signature (sig.asc).
- Evidence retrieval: compliance can request an evidence bundle (rotation records + syslog slice) via `redwoodctl evidences export --tenant <TENANT> --since <ISO>`; the CLI produces a time-limited signed tarball.

If GlobeBank wants, we can lock the rotation window during their business hours and run rotations in a 2am-4am maintenance window to minimize impact.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Alex —

Thanks for the quick review and good questions. A few action items before we finalize the SOW:

1) Compliance ask: please confirm the desired ephemeral TTL (options: 1h / 6h / 24h / 168h). We recommend 24h for balanced ops.
2) Evidence scope: confirm retention window for rotation artifacts (default 90 days). If you need >1 year we can expand to S3 archive and produce an updated pricing appendix.
3) Approval model: do you require multi-person root unseal / threshold-split for the HSM import? If yes, well add the KMIP/integration checklist to the runbook.

Jonas, can you add the exact CLI output example for `redwoodctl evidences export` in the runbook and a sample signed tarball filename pattern? Dylan, please attach the CLI examples you mentioned.

We can jump on a 30-minute call with GlobeBank compliance tomorrow if that helps — propose 9:00 AM PT if that works.

Best,
Soojin
